learner_operation: Solve a small consistent dependent linear system using Gauss-Jordan elimination, identify pivot/free variables, and select its full one-parameter vector solution. Read actual equation relationships to identify the complete affine solution line, not numerical formatting in answer options.

fixed_features.feature: Small consistent real linear systems with exactly one free variable
fixed_features.justification: Source tutorial and all supplied easy solving cases practice parametric dependent systems.

fixed_features.feature: Five-choice radio response and a worked Gauss-Jordan derivation
fixed_features.justification: All captured practice banks use this contract; no free-entry skill is introduced.

fixed_features.feature: A later pivot coordinate is constant when an earlier column is free
fixed_features.justification: RREF pivot definition makes its entries before the pivot zero; canonical free-y/pivot-z instance demonstrates this. This is mathematical structure, not incidental label fixing.

answer_roles.role: Free variable, pivot assignment and dimension/rank
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Free z or canonical free y; two-equation rank two in three variables or proportional three-equation rank one in two variables.
answer_roles.observed: All six justified cases occur in 36 fresh records; targeted free-y controls add 12 cases with multiple keys. Five runner records cover five cases.

answer_roles.role: Constant coordinates, zero intercepts and equal basic expressions
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Cancellation and equal-coordinate cases remain valid. A zero constant may be shared by all options if other coordinates distinguish solution lines.
answer_roles.observed: Earlier restrictions and new zero-constant boundary now accept; rational and all-zero boundaries are correctly printed and solved.

answer_roles.role: Which candidate line satisfies the system, including its visible coefficient shape
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Correct candidate and position can vary without a reserved integer, fraction, unit-coefficient or component-frequency signature.
answer_roles.observed: Default roles/positions vary, and the earlier fraction cue is repaired. However ordinary q-32244 always has correct slope -1, and its sole unmultiplied-y choice identifies the key in 8/8 applicable samples.

counterfactuals.change: Hold seed and all explicit parameters but first free coefficient fixed; change 2 to -2.
counterfactuals.expected: System, correct vector and explanation change; old vector becomes incorrect.
counterfactuals.observed: Exact printed-math checks and screenshot inspection agree; native grader rejects previous vector in changed record.
counterfactuals.justification: The free coefficient determines a basic-variable slope, an answer-bearing relationship.

counterfactuals.change: Hold RREF parameters and seed fixed; invertible row mixing changes mix[0] from 1 to -1.
counterfactuals.expected: Printed equations and row-operation route change; the complete solution line is preserved.
counterfactuals.observed: Printed prompt changed while keyed vector is equal; native grader accepts the previous visible vector.
counterfactuals.justification: Invertible row operations preserve the solution set, as taught by the source Gauss-Jordan method.

counterfactuals.change: Hold free_coefficients=[2,0], constants=[1,4] and mix=[1,1] fixed; change free_column from 1 to 2.
counterfactuals.expected: The role of y/z and the solution vector follow the changed coefficient columns.
counterfactuals.observed: Prompt and full vector differ consistently; exact bank checks and native all-choice grading pass for each.
counterfactuals.justification: Canonical source explicitly assigns free y and pivot z; default source variants often assign free z instead.

counterfactuals.change: Hold seed 82175, constants and mixing fixed; change first free coefficient from 1/2 to -1/2.
counterfactuals.expected: Printed system, solution vector and explanation change; the old vector is rejected.
counterfactuals.observed: Exact printed-math checks and actual native grader agree; rendered rational pair has different slopes, keys and worked RREF.
counterfactuals.justification: The changed coefficient determines the basic-coordinate slope; this is answer-bearing evidence.

counterfactuals.change: Hold seed 82175, rational RREF coefficients/constants fixed; change first invertible row mixing multiplier from 1 to -1.
counterfactuals.expected: Equations and route change while full solution is preserved.
counterfactuals.observed: Rendered prompt and row operations change; keyed vector is unchanged and old visible vector is accepted by the actual grader.
counterfactuals.justification: Elementary invertible row transformations preserve the solution set, the central source method.

shortcut_probes.cue: Sole unmultiplied parameter in first coordinate
shortcut_probes.subgroup: Recognizable rank-one two-variable systems with equal printed x/y coefficients (ordinary q-32244 sampling)
shortcut_probes.strategy: Ignore equations and constants; choose the only vector with y or -y instead of 2y,5y,etc. in its first coordinate.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Eight successes in eight applicable banks among twenty, versus 20% random choice on those same banks. The pool reserves minimum nonzero coefficient magnitude for the actual slope whenever other sampled slopes exceed one. This is not checking a vector against the equation, using coefficient ratios, or deriving the intercept; it is an incidental typographic action cue. Same counts before and after actual delivery filtering.

shortcut_probes.strategy: Choose the unique smallest first intercept.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Baseline is 20%. An apparent 4/4 predictor in the small fresh sample fails on controls (1/10); construction selects role before the system and permits all positions. This concern was expanded only because the initial sample appeared perfect.
